en: O heart that, bearing the effort, rises [and] is before [him]
you joining us, with peforming mouths, we shall store up
in woven words brought forth by tongues that have longing
the praise of him with flower colour who brought forth the good flower
We praise, we blame, we don’t praise, we don’t blame
we slight, we esteem, we don’t esteem, again we don’t slight
these, our Māl, red-eyed Māl, don’t you be furious
we of bad Karma, see, our Māl
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

en: Even though I know these, saying of them
these are not good, these are not bad, all these
cannot be approached or rejected by me. O lord
what is it that has to be done by me?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular, vocative

en: Who will have more praise than me afterwards, again
when one considers, apart from me who has much praise
having obtained my heart [to be] the servant of the great light
with an ocean-like nature, my Kaṇṇaṉ of black light?
The mother who got you, the father who begot you
who else are they? If you speak, how is it
that you who, for the traitress great in treachery to perish
put into [his] mouth [her] breast, father, show [us] the way?
Having shown the path, shall you dispell [us] from your side? Shall you
show [your] black dark sprout body? On a former day we did not know
What did you count on doing, Kaṇṇaṉ? Say it
If we do what, what shall we not suffer?
We, we of difficult Karma are far. Those of our heart
being close they have stopped approaching. Father
who dug up the earth, joining the flower-dwelling red lady to [your] chest
I shall approach your feet
We do not perceive with a clarity that gets near to [and] tastes you. Love
for you, it is great. What is this? Speak, you who possess the quality
that is drinking, you who measured the earth, you who have minuteness
difficult to see for the eyes of us sinners
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, second person, plural
pronominalised noun, first person, plural, oblique

en: What [is] painfully repeating “we are your servants” to him
who is great? Because he himself is difficult to approach, be by anything
for us now, see, heart, sit thinking by anything
on his account
Except for the twice Four, the One above the twice five
the once Four with eight, the once Two, for Tirumāl
who are we? Obeisance to whom, hey, alas, good heart?
We, ah, possess much fault
Is it strength in you to force, in a manner that he did not live
the sweet life of the strong Rakṣasa who by [his own] fault exerted himself in battle
you who stand as uncrying earth, you as sky, you as wind
you as fire and you as water?
Is it not that you have constantly suffered to be thrown down into weeping affliction?
What of going [and] saying anything? Go, heart? Even if instruction is given
you always take it firmly in hand. Praising
the feet of Kaṇṇaṉ, see, is the [right] practice
Except for falling off from that practice, when [your] servants want [something]
shall we see [them] lose [it] too, o lord, is there a loss?
And if you have taken us as servants, when I want [it] show [me]
by my eyes the complexion of your body
Being one who on the inside does not know by complexion the Black one, o heart
being a demon to the demoness who gave [her] breast [to him], who are you, going
although you know well [his] flesh, having tasted [his] sweet ornaments
looking out to stretch [your] hand into the hungry mouth of the serpent that is evil deed?
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, honorific

en: Having seen understand, having encountered give [yourself], o heart
once the misery that befalls [us] is destroyed there will be no talk of our perishing
in the greatness of [its] flood:
the excellence of him who slumbers with his red body, lying himself
while the body of the flood roars [and] strokes [his] feet
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person, honorific

en: Having been born from excellence, not growing out of superiority
at the time when [your] name was not [yet] Vāmāṉ, o great man, was it difficult
to accept water for the earth that you had embraced, for [your] chest to be full
eaten [and] spat out? Speak, you, for us to know encompassingly
He who, although at the time the servants around [him] wanted [it] he left [them alone]
not appearing, does not open his mouth even afterwards for those who have lived
he stretched out without measure [his] foot so that the strong heads of the Rakṣasa
crumbled like bright mountains all around
gloss: participial noun, third person, plural, imperfective aspect
perfective aspect, third person, masculine, singular

en: O knowing one who set forth all these many forms, not idle
as soon as he was involved in the snake’s being bound
so that that scar faded [that he had received] as soon as he had been bound
who knows your old form, speak?
There is no dearth of words, o heart that does not know the means
Without telling night from day, all the time look
you who see the one who protected, differently
the unique Five against all the great armies, in antiquity
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine, singular, accusative

en: When we enter into envisaging, [our] good heart that has taken knowledge in hand
is ashamed, isn’t it, when we [even] speak of going
[and] touching the sacred body of the excellent one
who accepted water for the earth, taking in in the form of a dwarf
Going there they are the narrow lane for my heart here today
in order to protect [it] from going to hot hell the feet stretched out
there that day by him of cloud colour so that the form of the earth
and the form of the water that surrounds the earth lay covered
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Such are the days that they wander about, for [their] feet to be perforated, [and] cry
Māl has entered my mind as an abode growing weary
without seeing a place where those with harsh deeds would sit in disctinction
with the expansiveness they prided themselves in before
‘You will be weary. Don’t let it weary you, heart’, I said
When [we] become weary Yama’s people will seize [us and], when we reach fatigue
they will bring [their] dogs [and] strike [us]
The one who will not let it be granted
who will grant he is mother [and] father [to us] for all [our] lives
gloss: negative, imperfective aspect, second person, singular
participial noun, imperfective aspect, masculine singular
negative, participial noun, imperfective aspect, masculine singular

en: He, he is a unique appearance. One without anything of his measure
is he. Also for others is his appearance. He
without fatigue he further ordains what is below and above earth. Therefore
who on earth can measure [him]?
When whoever is is does whatsoever, examining
[this] wide place, will there be accomplishing it? I have dispelled
the misery of the leader of [my] mind, full of excellence
I, through Kaṇṇaṉ, the leader of the groups of celestials
I and my heart have ceased acquiring bad Karma
in order to chase it away so that it enters forest and mountain
twitching under the stick that is called grace given by our lord
with a body dark as darkness itself
Was it joy that you crossed the earth with [your] foot or, if not that
was it joy that you measured the sky with [your] crown, long one
that day you went [and] measured without being able to know
the whole world, stretching out [your] foot with tight anklets?
That day our eye saw the cloud colour of the one with the discus
Although today there is existing without seeing [him], always
that form which is not seen by the physical eye will be perceived [and] seen
by the inner eye that is called the heart
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Is he easy to perceive for [any]one? When one directly
perceives our father on whom sways Tulsi in clusters
however many they are, they are easy [to perceive] for him. Therefore
our great lord here is easy [to perceive] for me
Here there is no sitting in disctinction, like formerly
The mind is small even for the excellence of my red-eyed Māl. There
without restraining [their] cloth [and] staying [my] harsh deeds further
lifting [their] feet, is it not beauty?
Being such as know the beauty and the shade of each foot
of him who ends [our] harsh Karma, we have become
his, the one’s who resided on the vast ocean that day
having danced with the pot lifted upon [his] head, so as to spin it
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Tāmōtaraṉ is one who wants [people] to be servant to him
Without doing it when they are told “do servantship to him”, they are people
with hearts that have the degradation of the bad deeds they do, saying “ours”
What is our doing here in this place?
If one knows anything, if one rejoices in him, what
is the way not to get close, accepting everything
to him who has brought into just ruin
with [his] discus], the Asuras who clearly did not do anything?
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, locative

en: As soon as we heard of your nature of lying on the milk ocean
[our] feet faltered, [our] heart softened, [our] eyes span, oh you with the light
of the blue ocean, you beginning, you of right conduct who chases the old deeds
away from us, standing close to you
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, vocative, second person
pronominalised noun, second person, singular, vocative

en: Standing, sitting, lying and roaming about
he cannot cease from anyone, he does not depart from my heart
he who dug the chest, breaking the mouth of the gold-coloured one
with the strong side of [his] palm that day, he possesse love [towards us], isn’t it?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine, singular
perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine singular

en: “He is that one, he is this one, he is the one there, [or] again he is
the one beyond”, without constantly saying so, if, understanding that
he is that one, one is not separated from Kaṇṇaṉ alone
he is who ever he may be
There being those who posses knowledge of the way it is, is it not rare?
It is us who possess that, good heart. That which is praise of Māl
with cool Tulsi joined by honeymakers that graze on flowers
is [our] duty. Do it with love!
There is the time to do it, if we are who, heart
the time to blink? Even if it is abusing [him] about the matters
of trouble with the shepherdess, just speaking about Māyaṉ
with the productive Tulsi drive away [your] faults
gloss: proper name, pronominalised noun, singular, masculine

en: Did we make an effort so as to fail, o heart? Speak
one time invoking the one with thriving Tulsi on [his] chest
going, without taking help to flourish, [to fail] the opportunity
that take the help of the mouth, that is, praise of him?
As for an opportunity like this, there will be no other, come heart
Don’t go [and] incite [and] make [me] enter into hot hell
Force the praise of him who, drinking the milk as life nectar
of the demon mother with fiery milk, put an end to her life
gloss: perfective aspect, participial noun, masculine, singular, accusative

en: Bending, so that they crumbled, the strong heads
of the wrestlers who faced [you], having come thinking “we are strong”
you would thrash them with your strong golden-discus hand. Without being torn
this earth will stand for many days
“He ate the earth, he spit out the earth, he dug up the earth, he measured the earth
he who before created the place that is the earth”, the say indeed. Because he also is
the place for the earth, who is the place?
Those will not enter him who is for any other
gloss: singular, masculine, third person, perfective aspect
singular, masculine, third person, pronominalised noun

en: [Him] who, on behalf of the gods come thinking [him to be] the refuge
causes evil to tremble, is there, for those who do not keep seating [and]
praising him, for [their] unbifurcated minds to be elevated
a way to destroy [their] minds’ misery?
gloss: participial noun, causative, imperfective aspect, masculine, singular
negative, perfective aspect, pronominalised noun, honorific, dative

en: Even though one says the good heart and the mouth possessing a tongue
joined in [that] way very befittingly will not fall this, isn’t it?
for those who keep not praising Māl, very befittingly
is the deed they do further
Fearing the heat those with [bad] karma strive to give
without thinking to swerve even a little that is [the size of] a millet’s [grain]
with [my] speech I have praised the golden feet of the leader
to whom the celestials bow in worship
Thus far the words I speak: day after day
think, heart what is the way for you
to guard [us] from joining hot hell, that is the way
not abandoned, red-eyed Māl, he who has the colour of water from the rising flood
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, neuter singular
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Even if you have come to think human beings, thinking [of you
and] bowing, will beg for something, there is no need. To think straight
[of you and] bow, how many, in which place are they, Māl? And that itself
how much is it to us?
For ourselves we have achieved liberation that is at the height
of the heavenly land that, isn’t it, is the way it is directing
[our] mind towards him who killed cruel-horned bulls, seven together
for the sake of her with soft shoulder luxuriant [like] bamboo
A cloud, a vast mountain, the dark sea, ample darkness
a flower not left alone by bees, another thing when we see them
whenever it sees the colour of monsoon clouds [our] heart runs
separating from us in the thought “it is Kaṇṇaṉ’s great form”
Those with minds that, separating, without looking at anything
roam about after him, will he not long for them one time
[and], ah, feel pity for them, alas? Is it [that] hard
the heart of him who split the horse[‘s mouth]?
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, neuter singular
participial noun, perfective aspect, third person

en: Having mastered the anger of those who are strongly fortified
the once Five that master the mind, [and] joined them in one place
seeing the feet of him with cool Tulsi from the fields, isn’t it
is the honour that creates the excellence that stirs liberally.(?)
To see the singular form of him who that day begged for the earth
having contemplated honour, who ate, having contemplated it as food
the poison of the deceitful one
without our eye having desire to see any other thing, will [our] mouth
have anything to eat without revering [his] excellence?
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine singular
participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine singular, genitive

en: There is something, red-eyed Māl, I have to say. Thinking
“what shall I do” for your servants, you may start [something]. In all their minds
that are directed on your fame, is there anything else as sweet
[even] the heaven that you may grant them with Vaikuntam?
Whether in the sky, the sea, the wind, inside the fire
or in the forest, alltogether we don’t see, we who have humbled ourselves
before the feet of him who brought down the fruit by throwing, for it to be high
the calf born by a cow, on [any] side, ah, [our] harsh misery
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, third person, honorific
participial noun, perfective aspect, first person, plural

en: Even though it is difficult to come to the side of him
whose bed is a sapphire snake where the flood whispers on the side
together for us there is always seeing him with the mind
the coming of him wo ends the sorrows of the mind
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person, honorific

en: There is no way to come living is sweet indeed, ah
[but] the way shown by the cowherd who changes the fear
of the path not to be entered by anyone as a path, by him who is far
by the mother of the world on that day, by the tricky one
Will he not change the harsh deeds established on the way, heart?
Māl who took the war Asura in an embrace [and], bending [and] seizing
lowered sides everywhere so that a flood of [his] flesh lept up
dug up the chest, so that the life was subdued
Māl, don’t change the effulgence of [your] body. Now I
settled in ripening in your milk-like excellence. It is not
furtheron obtaining the absence of birth [and] doing service under [your] foot
I want, [but] the good of absence of forgetting
Thinking there will be their getting to come [back] to the place the harsh deeds
won’t take themselves in hand(?) in the forest or wherever going in the middle
while [we?] retreat [and] think of reciting the names of the great man
who closes his eyes on the waves spilled by the battling flood
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person

en: Come back, don’t look at anything, stand behind the Dark one with
productive Tulsi [or] rush forth without standing, my heart. Turning anywhere
for protecting [us] from joining the old big hot hell
there is no other lord, see
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, second person

en: That day the lord in sequence measured the earth on [his] red feet
if those from the heavenly land had joined in the order of the Vedas
[and] strewn flowers shining with pollen turn after turn, would they not resemble
the very stars that lie shining above, on the hanging sky?
The one who measured the earth stretching himself like a unique
sapphire shaft for the indestructible pure umbrella called sky
with a silver cover called emptiness on spokes called stars
afterwards he is the great remedy for our diseases
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

ta: பின் துரக்குங் காற்றிழந்த சூற்கொண்டல் பேர்ந்தும் போய்
en: Turning back the cloud, with pregancy lost by the wind that drives it from behind
has its true form that comes close into the strong waves in the Highest one
who that day sawed off the nose and big ears of the evil Rakṣasi
with [his] sacred just discus
If they considered that he was the highest
would the hands of the immortals not join [and] worship
with strength, once three times, the one who that day
shot the seven trees, the one who tore the bird’s mouth?
gloss: participial noun, perfective aspect, masculine singular, accusative
participial noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person

en: The severe sorrow that mixes with [and] afflicts us, heart
he will fatally overcome and fold it up. Always
wear a word garland for mountain-like old Māl
for Kēcavaṉ, for Nāraṇaṉ, for Mātavaṉ
The Dark one who by his discus that was hot, made the life
of the old Rakṣasa a misery in that place, the Veda [expert]
with cool Tulsi that has taken a vigorous scent, o heart
know [him], see. I have said that
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

en: As for the pretty desirable world, if you want it, thinking it is good
it is without value, isn’t it? Leaving it behind
foolish heart that constantly joins the earth although it says “I am [his] servant”
learn by praising Kaṇṇaṉ’s feet
Stone and sounding sea and the heavenly land Vaikunta
have they become emptily desolate, o evil? Victoriously
the Tall one, the one black in colour has entered inside [and] does not leave
the inside of the mind of me who am [his] servant
gloss: perfective aspect, third person, neuter plural

en: [My] harsh deeds have become such as whose eyes have reddened inside
it is that [their] faces decay, isn’t it?, strained. Me with thoughts
that are stored in the ocean of excellence of increasing Tirumāl
for whom is there straight oppressing [and] killing me?
gloss: participial noun, imperfective aspect, third person

en: The one with a crown of thick gold, the one with the thousand names
the one with the glow-absorbing glowing discus I who have adopted
him as mother and father who chase away affliction, for my mind
if there be what, what now?
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, accusative, third person
participial noun, singular, first person, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, genitive, first person

en: Standing here now what shall I tell about your greatness?
Form without support who stands alone, the one of red matted hair
with the dewy water moving inside is in [your] body, the one
with four faces [has his] origin in your navel
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: The holy forms that were the beginning are three, they say. Only one
of the three was the beginning, they say. O First one
you of equally shining cloud form, is it not inside you
the flower of the tawny shining lotus?
Bilberry, ironwood, blue lotus, flowering
water-lilies whenever I see such blossoms the soft soul
[and] body of me evil-doer are very full, thinking that all those
are the forms of the lord
If I beg always, without leaving off a single day
he won’t feel any compassion, he won’t show [his] form, the cowherd lord
who protected the cows with the hill as umbrella. O heart
a great place it is, the earth
The earth and the vast sky are inside you. You, having entered
by the way of my ear, are not inside me. Except in annihilation
who will know [how] to say I am great, you are great?
You with the flesh-drinking discus, reflect
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, second person, negative
verbal noun, pronominalised noun, masculine singular, accusative

en: When I think of [you my] mind enlarges and when I open my eyes
[and] truly behold you, so that the masses of Karma crack, I too
will be one who is of the measure of the world. What [is this]
o form that measured they world, tell [me]
gloss: imperfective aspect, third person, masculine singular

en: When talking about it, who are those that could be said to have kinsmen
my father who lies on the roaring ocean? In all the sayings
I am without any other but you as a support that is
the benefit of a word for my life
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect
pronominalised noun, singular, genitive, first person

en: Even if we were to have companions, days, many relatives
an old family, the aid of a retinue and daily pleasures, absorb
as unceasing food, good heart, the ancient excellence of the Cārṅka bearer
whose work does not cease, with arrows on the string
Will it not be a light in the inner land, will it fear maturing Karma
will it admire the heavenly land as one the birth that is as a servant
to the great cowherd with the discus in [his] palm
whoever it may be [and] however lowly
Even if we were to have the pleasure to abandon other births
old age [and] sickness [and] moreover to go beyond, in all oblivion
would I count a day of not praising the feet of him who measured
the world other than affliction?
gloss: participial noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: Without regarding whether it is day [or] night he will
with hostility rule us both times, he will not consider
that these are unfit slaves, without support because of excellence
the resident of the ample expanse, understandingly
All days are base of me staying behind silently, me with evil deeds
in the absence of any perception with understanding [days] occupied
without praising the father with the discus in [his] palm who that day
followed after that deer, having hidden in [another] form
Forget [or] don’t forget, heart. I said
this is the way we shall escape, see. [Things] that are not
to be done you may do, heart, I’m afraid
praising the one with hard work on the wrestlers’ day
gloss: participial noun, singular, second person, perfective aspect

en: When [I] say “praise, adorn his feet with flowers, lower your head
fold [your] two hands”, they do not fold. Rules in ruin
without praising him “where have you been?”, my heart
ieven if it is staying, stay
As ones that have made ceaseless efforts, spreading over the lowered sky
entering where have they done which penance the clouds that take
the good colour from our Kaṇṇaṉ who closes his eyes
on the cool milk ocean in the foaming flood
Those who don’t go about thinking of words blended with excellence [such as]
“he with a body blended with cloud [colour], the one with a discus blended with [his] hand
the one with a strong belly blended with the earth, the one on the snake bed”
thinking of what will they go now into the deep sorrow of pervasive Karma?
gloss: pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person
pronominalised noun, singular, masculine, third person

en: All this time and again now, if you stand a little
always speak only this, my heart. Always
strive to praise but the true anklet of him who chases away the Karma on me
the one with the discus that does not get loose from [his] hand
gloss: pronominalised noun, third person, masculine singular
